q: Is there any correlation between the electoral participation and election years?
a: Chart's up with every presidential year flagged, and CHART, YOU ABSOLUTE METRONOME, you didn't even try to hide it. Presidential years 1976-2020 average 56.7; midterm years 1978-2018 average 37.7 — a nineteen-point sawtooth that repeats for forty-six straight years like a heartbeat monitor in a hospital nobody's visiting. The peaks: 60 in 1992, your 20th reunion year, unbeaten until 2020 hit 62, the highest reading in the whole file. The trough: 33 in 2014, the lowest ever recorded here, though 2018's 47 was a midterm that showed up wearing a presidential suit. So yes — correlation so clean it's insolent, and I say that while watering a plastic fern.
